introduction: In the 19th century, Indian society was plagued by superstitions and social evils like Sati, untouchability, and child marriage. Influenced by Western education and modern rationalism, several Indian thinkers took the initiative to reform society and religion. This era is widely known as the 'Indian Renaissance'.

core_concepts.title: Brahmo Samaj (1828)
core_concepts.description: Founded by Raja Rammohan Roy. Its main objective was to eliminate idol worship, the Sati system, and polytheism from Hinduism, promoting 'Monotheism' (belief in one God).

core_concepts.title: Arya Samaj (1875)
core_concepts.description: Founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in Bombay. He gave the slogan 'Go back to Vedas'. The Samaj strongly opposed the birth-based caste system and untouchability.

core_concepts.title: Ramakrishna Mission (1897)
core_concepts.description: Founded by Swami Vivekananda in memory of his guru, Ramakrishna Paramahansa. Its core philosophy was 'Service to mankind is service to God'.

core_concepts.title: Satyashodhak Samaj (1873)
core_concepts.description: Founded by Jyotiba Phule in Maharashtra. Its objective was to liberate lower castes (Dalits) and women from Brahmanical dominance and exploitation, and to spread education among them.

important_entities.name: Raja Rammohan Roy
important_entities.significance: Due to his relentless efforts, Governor-General Lord William Bentinck declared the 'Sati' practice illegal in 1829.

important_entities.name: Swami Vivekananda
important_entities.key_fact: Parliament of the World's Religions in Chicago (1893)
important_entities.significance: He established the greatness of Vedanta and Indian philosophy on the global stage. His birthday (January 12) is celebrated as 'National Youth Day'.

important_entities.name: Swami Dayanand Saraswati
important_entities.significance: He initiated the 'Shuddhi Movement' to bring back those who had converted from Hinduism to other religions.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Brahmo Samaj was highly influenced by Western education and modern ideas, whereas Arya Samaj was entirely based on the 'Infallibility of the Vedas' and was highly critical of Western culture.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Roy's Brahmo, Dayanand's Arya, Viveka's Ramakrishna
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A simple association to remember: Raja Rammohan Roy (Brahmo Samaj), Dayanand Saraswati (Arya Samaj), Vivekananda (Ramakrishna Mission).

exam_strategy_tips: Questions asking you to 'Match the following' for social organizations and their founders are extremely common.
Memorize the year the Sati system was abolished (1829) and the Governor-General responsible for it (Lord William Bentinck).
